risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company's activities expose it primarily to financial risks from changes in foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates due to foreign currency borrowings and variable interest loans; the Company has not entered into derivative contracts to manage its foreign currency risk or risks related to anticipated sales and purchases.
- The textile business is exposed to volatility in raw material prices, particularly yarn and fabric inputs, which can impact margins in export operations.
- Intense competition from domestic and international players poses a challenge to maintaining pricing power and market share; the FMCG segment faces increasing competition from established brands and new entrants requiring continuous innovation and strong brand positioning.
- Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments, and changes in trade policies can affect export demand and supply chain stability for the Company's textile and cosmetics export segments.
- Rising input costs, including packaging and logistics, may impact profitability of the FMCG (Cosmetics) segment.
- Regulatory changes, compliance requirements, and evolving quality standards across markets require ongoing adaptation in both the textile and FMCG businesses.
- The Company is exposed to credit risk from operating activities (primarily trade receivables) and from financing activities including bank deposits and foreign exchange transactions; customer credit quality is assessed and monitored under an established credit risk policy.
- The Company faces liquidity risk — the risk that it may not be able to meet present and future cash and collateral obligations without incurring unacceptable losses — and manages this through close monitoring of its liquidity position and cash management system.
